news.title: CorWave Completes Enrollment in Feasibility Study and Presents First Clinical Data on Adaptive Support with its Wave Membrane LVAD
news.summary: CorWave announced completion of enrollment in its LVAS feasibility study at two centers in Australia and Kazakhstan. Its release describes adaptive-support observations in a presented case; aggregate feasibility results remain forthcoming. The wave-membrane pump is investigational.

news.title: Mount Sinai to Lead National Trial of Targeted Therapy for Infants With Noonan Syndrome and Severe Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
news.summary: Mount Sinai announced it will lead BabyMERIT, a multicentre trial of trametinib in infants (older than 28 days, younger than 6 months) with Noonan syndrome or a closely related RASopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and severe heart failure needing hospital admission. Per the release, 25 infants will be treated for 12 months in a single-arm, open-label design and compared with a real-world cohort of about 100 infants given standard care since 2015; the primary endpoint is death, heart transplantation or septal myectomy by 12 months. The registry (last updated 2026-09-14) lists Phase 3, not yet recruiting, estimated start August 2027.

additionalSources.label: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07817186, Baby MERIT (API record opened 2026-10-22; first posted 2026-09-14)

news.title: FDA Approval of Edwards Lifesciences' PASCAL Precision System Opens New Treatment Pathway for Patients With Tricuspid Valve Disease
news.summary: Edwards says the FDA approved its PASCAL Precision system for tricuspid edge-to-edge repair, indicated to improve quality of life and functional status in symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation despite optimal medical therapy, at intermediate or greater surgical risk and judged suitable by a heart team (FDA label not read). An executive says the PASCAL system has been available in the US for degenerative mitral regurgitation for several years; the release does not say if that covers Precision. It also mentions a recent undated approval of PASCAL Ace with Capture Clarity for degenerative mitral TEER, and one-year CLASP IITR data at TCT.

additionalSources.label: TCTMD, FDA Green-lights Pascal System for Tricuspid Valve Repair (trade press)
Cardiac Interventions Today, Pascal Precision approved for tricuspid repair (trade press)
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04097145, CLASP II TR pivotal trial (names the PASCAL System, not Precision)

news.title: Noah Labs announces first VOICE-HF participants
news.summary: Noah Labs announced the first participants in VOICE-HF, a prospective study of its investigational Vox voice-analysis software in stage C chronic heart failure. The trial is intended to test worsening-HF detection from daily home recordings; no trial outcomes or marketing authorization are established by the announcement.

news.title: The PALMETTO Study: Palmetto vAlve for Lifelong Management of patiEnts With miTral Valve regurgiTatiOn
news.summary: ClinicalTrials.gov first posted PALMETTO on 2026-10-21: the sponsor, ReValve Solutions, registers a prospective, single-arm, multicenter early feasibility study of its investigational ReValve System for transcatheter mitral valve replacement in symptomatic primary or secondary mitral regurgitation, for patients whose surgical risk is high but not prohibitive and whom the heart team deems anatomically or technically unsuited to TEER. The record lists 10 estimated participants, one US site, status Not yet recruiting and an estimated November 2026 start. A registration is not enrollment; no results or device design details are given.

news.title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
news.summary: A retrospective multicentre study applied a deep-learning pipeline to preprocedural noncontrast CT in 915 TAVR patients included from 2014 to 2023 (median age 84; 160 deaths, 17.5%, over a median 22 months). Mortality was higher with lower subcutaneous fat volume and higher adipose-tissue attenuation, and lower with greater skeletal-muscle volume and attenuation. Adding the body-composition measures to demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors raised Harrell C from 0.66 to 0.71; this shows association and discrimination, not a tested clinical use.

news.title: Percutaneous Multivalvular Endocarditis Debulking With a Whole-Body Embolic Protection Device
news.summary: A JACC: Case Reports paper of two patients reports, to the authors' knowledge, the first use of whole-body embolic protection during percutaneous debulking of aortic and combined tricuspid/mitral endocarditis. The authors call the Emboliner filter investigational, note it had previously been studied in transcatheter aortic valve replacement, and used it as an adjunct to AngioVac in one patient with aortic valve and one with combined tricuspid and mitral endocarditis. They report over 90% of the vegetation removed and no embolic event during the procedure or hospital stay; two cases allow no comparison or rate.

news.title: VERINA: A Phase IV Prospective Multicenter Study of Vericiguat in Indian Patients with Worsening Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction
news.summary: VERINA, a single-arm, open-label phase IV study, gave vericiguat on top of foundational therapy to 205 Indian adults with chronic HFrEF who had experienced a worsening heart-failure episode (203 in the full analysis set), followed for about 48 weeks. At week 48 Kaplan-Meier estimates were 10.1% for cardiovascular death or first heart-failure hospitalization and 3.3% for cardiovascular death; 91.6% attained the target dose, drug-related adverse events were 3.4%, and no new safety signal was observed. There is no comparator.

news.title: Safety and Efficacy of a Novel Balloon Angiographic Catheter for Coronary Venography During Left Ventricular Lead Implantation: A Prospective Multicenter Single-arm Trial
news.summary: PRELIMINARY (preprint). A Research Square preprint reports a prospective, single-arm, four-centre trial of the LeesCa balloon angiographic catheter for coronary venography during coronary-sinus left ventricular lead implantation: 97 patients, device success 97/97 against a predefined 93% target, immediate procedural success 98.97%, three mild adverse events (3.09%), follow-up to discharge or 7 days. Manufacturer and regulatory status are not stated in the abstract, which gives registry number ChiCTR2400089647 (not opened).

news.title: Ultrasound-Guided versus Fluoroscopy-Guided Femoral Access for Structural Heart Procedures: Outcomes From Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Left Atrial Appendage Closure
news.summary: A single-centre retrospective cohort of 165 consecutive patients having transfemoral TAVI (93) or LAAC (72) in 2022-2024 compared ultrasound-guided with conventional puncture; ultrasound was used in 34.5%. Haemoglobin fell less with ultrasound in both venous and arterial access. After 1:1 propensity matching of arterial cases (31 per group), complications were 3.2% with ultrasound versus 29.0% without; in the venous cohort the difference (3.8% vs 17.4%) was not significant (p=0.143).

news.title: Treatment selection and long-term survival in patients aged 50 to < 75 years undergoing valve reintervention for failed surgical aortic bioprostheses: insights from the Netherlands Heart Registration
news.summary: In the Netherlands Heart Registration, 345 patients aged 50 to under 75 with a failed surgical aortic bioprosthesis (2015-2020) received valve-in-valve TAVI (41%) or redo surgical aortic valve replacement (59%). ViV-TAVI went to older, higher-risk patients; Kaplan-Meier survival estimates at 4 years were 74.4% after ViV-TAVI and 88.4% after redo-SAVR (89.6% and 89.8% at 2 years). The authors describe the study as observational and say it cannot show that either strategy is better.

news.title: Anatomy-Driven Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair of the Systemic Atrioventricular Valve in Complex Transposition Anatomy
news.summary: A single-centre series of four consecutive high-risk adults (two with congenitally corrected transposition, two after atrial-switch repair) describes transcatheter edge-to-edge repair of the systemic atrioventricular valve, using PASCAL ACE in three and MitraClip in one. Implantation succeeded in all four, regurgitation fell from severe to mild and no major acute complications occurred. The authors suggest right internal jugular access when inferior venous anatomy is absent or likely to give unfavourable curvature, and present the cases as technique notes, not comparative evidence of efficacy or safety.

news.title: Prognostic Impact of Moderate Secondary Mitral Regurgitation After Optimized Medical Therapy in Heart Failure
news.summary: Among 2,468 ambulatory heart-failure patients with echocardiography at baseline and again after 12 months of optimized guideline-directed therapy, 15.6% had moderate and 3.9% severe mitral regurgitation at 12 months. Over a median 6.9 years, moderate MR was independently associated with a higher risk of death or first heart-failure hospitalization (HR 1.69) and of all-cause death (HR 1.54); severe MR carried HR 1.81 for the composite. This is an observational prognostic analysis and does not evaluate mitral intervention.

news.title: Dapagliflozin in phenotypically stratified HFpEF without myocardial fibrosis: the STADIA-HFpEF randomized crossover trial
news.summary: In a 34-week double-blind crossover against placebo (32 randomized, 29 completed; median age 73, 88% women), dapagliflozin 10 mg showed no significant difference from placebo in the co-primary measures of left ventricular distensibility (E/e'/LVEDVi) and relaxation (mean e') in HFpEF patients phenotyped with a multi-level work-up, including cardiac MRI, to exclude structural cardiomyopathies and significant myocardial fibrosis (extracellular-matrix remodeling). Most secondary measures showed no clear change; an isolated improvement in left atrial conduit strain and numerical falls in inflammatory biomarkers are described as exploratory.
news.sourceName: European Heart Journal - Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy (PubMed record)

news.title: LAAO design review, Part 1: Device architectures and the allocation of four functions
news.summary: An engineering review of how left atrial appendage occlusion devices deliver, seal, hold, and heal. Part 1 compares architectures and their functional dependencies, with original diagrams and documentary sources.

news.title: News Insights | October 3–16, 2026
news.summary: Two distinct delivery-system safety notices identify deployment and retrieval constraints. The CLASP II TR design paper sets a separate question about interpreting a forthcoming hierarchical endpoint.

news.title: FDA issues early alert for specified Commander M delivery-system lots
news.summary: FDA's October 15 Early Alert concerns four Commander M delivery-system lots used with SAPIEN M3. Edwards' October 5 letter reports three balloon bursts; as of that date, one associated death and one serious injury were reported. Burst balloons may prevent retrieval and require surgery in patients unsuitable for surgery. The public notice provides no exposure denominator or confirmed root cause; it does not assign a recall class.

additionalSources.label: FDA CDRH update index (October 15 alert date)

news.title: News Insights | September 30–October 13, 2026
news.summary: Analysis of pediatric follow-up, validation boundaries across three modeling studies, and new CardioMEMS patient-facing capabilities.

news.title: Cytokinetics reports additional ACACIA-HCM analyses presented at HFSA
news.summary: Cytokinetics reported additional ACACIA-HCM analyses at HFSA, covering composite exercise performance, responder domains, dose titration and safety in non-obstructive HCM. The written release is sponsor reporting; the underlying HFSA abstracts were not located. Non-obstructive use remains investigational, distinct from the approved adult obstructive-HCM indication; the release also reports systolic dysfunction and heart-failure events.

additionalSources.label: HFSA 2026 late-breaking program (presentation titles and schedule)

news.title: BridgeBio reports an independent EHR comparison of acoramidis and tafamidis in ATTR-CM
news.summary: BridgeBio announced HFSA presentation of an independent retrospective Epic COSMOS electronic-health-record comparison of patients newly initiating acoramidis or tafamidis, reporting an association between acoramidis and lower adverse-outcome rates. This sponsor-disclosed observational result is not a randomized head-to-head treatment effect; residual confounding and limited follow-up remain, and the full study was described as under journal peer review. Quantitative outcomes are omitted pending an accessible original study or abstract.

additionalSources.label: HFSA-hosted copy of the BridgeBio announcement
Earlier peer-reviewed Komodo claims analysis (distinct dataset and study)
HFSA announcement of the planned presentations (October 6)

news.title: Cardurion reports dose-dependent HFrEF biomarker results for tovinontrine; HFpEF trial misses NT-proBNP signal
news.summary: Cardurion reported that investigational PDE9 inhibitor tovinontrine reduced NT-proBNP at two lower doses in the Phase 2 CYCLE-1 REF HFrEF trial, with no benefit at the highest dose. CYCLE-2 PEF found no significant NT-proBNP change at that dose in HFpEF. These sponsor-reported biomarker findings do not establish hospitalization or survival benefit.

news.title: Affinia announces HFSA presentation featuring AFTX-201 and UPBEAT BAG3 DCM trial
news.summary: Affinia announced an HFSA 2026 oral presentation on AFTX-201 and its Phase 1/2 UPBEAT trial in BAG3-associated DCM, scheduled October 10, and a company-sponsored event on October 11. The release describes an investigational program and trial population; its animal-model statements are preclinical and are not evidence of human benefit.

news.title: Bayer schedules REVEAL early-detection post-hoc analysis at HFSA
news.summary: Bayer announced an October 11 late-breaking post-hoc REVEAL analysis about possible early cardiac amyloidosis detection. The page is dated October 9 with an October 8 release dateline. No inspected written HFSA result abstract supports new outcome numbers.

news.title: CLASP II TR design paper outlines PASCAL comparison with medical therapy
news.summary: The CLASP II TR design paper describes a 450-participant randomized comparison of PASCAL repair plus medical therapy with medical therapy alone for symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation. Its six-month hierarchical endpoint combines clinical events and quality of life. The randomized trial completed enrollment; primary results are expected and are not reported.

news.title: Patient-specific simulations compare ventricular flow energetics in calcific and rheumatic mitral stenosis
news.summary: A fluid–structure simulation study compared one healthy, one calcific and one rheumatic patient-derived mitral geometry. The calcific case imposed greater modeled ventricular flow-energy burden than the rheumatic case at equivalent cardiac outputs. These proof-of-concept models lack subvalvular structures and direct in-vivo validation; they do not establish patient outcomes or implant performance.

news.title: FDA posts Class II recall for specified Trilogy delivery-catheter lots
news.summary: FDA posted three size-specific records for one Class II Trilogy delivery-catheter recall event, covering specified 23-, 25-, and 27-mm catheter lots. The firm initiated the action July 31; sleeve-liner separation may cause difficulty or inability to deploy the valve. FDA lists a nonconforming material/component and quarantine/return instructions. Quantities in commerce describe inventory, not treated patients or failure rates.

news.title: Pediatric ASD study reports six-month right-heart remodeling after transcatheter closure
news.summary: A prospective observational study followed 53 children after secundum ASD closure with Amplatzer or Occlutech Figulla Flex II devices. Right-heart measures improved at six months, with functional changes concentrated in defects at least 10 mm. The uncontrolled, single-center findings do not compare the devices or establish long-term benefit.

news.title: Abbott announces CardioGuide HF patient pressure access and treatment-plan updates
news.summary: Abbott announced FDA approval for CardioMEMS system updates that let care teams enable patient access to pulmonary artery pressure trends and send clinician-configured medication instructions through CardioGuide HF. Availability is planned later in 2026. The release does not identify a software build or establish additional clinical benefit; the decision-specific FDA record remains unverified.

news.title: EchoDino preprint evaluates pediatric-trained echocardiography representations across age groups
news.summary: A preprint first submitted October 4 and revised October 7 describes EchoDino, trained on 3.7 million frames from 1.7 million unlabeled pediatric echo videos and evaluated across nine pediatric/adult datasets. The abstract reports structural-heart-disease detection AUC 0.872 versus 0.811 for a comparator. This is model evaluation, with no established clinical deployment or point-of-care utility.

news.title: Emboline reports first US commercial Emboliner use and begins a controlled launch
news.summary: Emboline reported two commercial Emboliner procedures during TAVR at Columbia on October 1 and announced a controlled US launch on October 2. FDA lists EPC-03 clearance under K261715 on September 8. Commercial use is a separate milestone from clearance; the release does not provide comparative stroke-prevention outcomes or demonstrate broad availability.

news.title: Preprint validates a TAVR fluid–structure model against a pulse duplicator
news.summary: An arXiv preprint compares simulated flow, pressure and leaflet dynamics with pulse-duplicator measurements at 60, 70 and 80 bpm. Boundary parameters were calibrated at 70 bpm and held fixed, while measured pressure and flow informed forcing at each rate. Agreement supports conditional bench validation and parameter transfer; it does not establish in-vivo or patient-specific prediction.

news.title: FDA approves AUTUS size-adjustable surgical pulmonary valve for pediatric patients
news.summary: FDA approved the AUTUS Size-Adjustable Valve through PMA for pediatric congenital pulmonary valve disease on October 1. Initial implantation is surgical; later balloon expansion can widen the polymeric-leaflet valve from approximately 13 mm to as much as 22 mm. FDA describes a 62-patient study but cautions that expansion experience is limited. Exact approved labeling and the PMA identifier remain to be reviewed.

news.title: Daxor announced HFSA exhibition and two scheduled blood-volume analysis ePosters
news.summary: Daxor announced an exhibit of its next-generation blood-volume analyzer at HFSA 2026 and listed two independent-investigator ePosters scheduled for October 10 on LVAD/total-artificial-heart patients and advanced-heart-failure volume phenotypes. The announcement supplies presentation titles and schedule, not poster results or a device model identifier; no poster document was located in this review.

news.title: FDA expands CAMZYOS indication to pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg
news.summary: FDA expanded mavacamten’s US indication to adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg with symptomatic obstructive HCM, to improve functional capacity and symptoms. The expansion followed evaluation of pediatric patients in SCOUT-HCM. The approved weight threshold is distinct from trial age eligibility; echocardiographic monitoring and REMS requirements continue.

news.title: Cytokinetics announces start of ASPEN-HCM real-world study of aficamten
news.summary: Cytokinetics announced ASPEN-HCM, a prospective observational study of aficamten in adults with symptomatic obstructive HCM in routine practice. Planned measures cover safety, clinical outcomes, patient-reported health and resource use; these are study objectives, not results. A study-specific registry identifier and current enrollment were not verified in this review.

additionalSources.label: MYQORZO prescribing information (adult symptomatic oHCM indication)

news.title: Mitria partners with T45 Labs to advance investigational Subvalvular Spacer
news.summary: Mitria announced a T45 Labs partnership and named Marwan Berrada-Sounni CEO to advance its investigational Subvalvular Spacer for secondary/functional MR. The release reports six recipients but does not define device builds, surgical versus transcatheter composition, or a registry cohort. SVS remains unavailable for commercial sale; the cumulative sponsor count is not a clinical efficacy result.

news.title: Puerarin-loaded artificial-plasma coating shows preclinical valve-material effects
news.summary: An Acta Biomaterialia study describes a hydroxyethyl-starch hydrogel coating on glutaraldehyde-crosslinked porcine pericardium, with ROS-responsive puerarin release. The abstract reports reduced platelet/protein adhesion, endothelial-cell support and reduced calcification at 12 weeks in rat subcutaneous implants. This is a distinct strategy from the earlier diclofenac nanogel report; human valve durability is not established. Only the abstract was reviewed.

news.title: Preprint models mitral valve dynamics and single- versus double-clip TEER
news.summary: An arXiv preprint models a reconstructed human mitral valve, including blood-flow interaction and idealized single- and double-clip repairs. A penalty constraint enforces leaflet coaptation without modeling the clip itself. Reconstruction checks and mesh-convergence tests support the computational method; its repair scenarios are simulations, not clinical outcomes or validated patient-specific treatment recommendations.

news.title: FDA clears Tempus ECG-MR software to flag signs associated with moderate or severe mitral regurgitation
news.summary: FDA cleared Tempus ECG-MR through 510(k) K254297 on September 25. The prescription software analyzes eligible resting 12-lead ECGs from patients 65 or older at cardiovascular risk and returns a binary flag to support follow-up. It is not diagnostic, does not rule out MR, and is not for paced ECGs or serial monitoring. FDA’s summary reports retrospective validation in 6,341 ECGs across four US sites, with 75% sensitivity and 70% specificity; predictive values depend on prevalence.

news.title: Health Canada posts Amulet labeling recall for pulmonary artery injury precautions
news.summary: Health Canada published a Type II labeling recall for eight original Amulet 9-ACP2 models on September 25, with a recall date of September 10. The notice concerns a revised pulmonary-artery contraindication and landing-zone distance assessment; it explicitly states that the notification is unrelated to device defectiveness. FDA separately approved the US labeling change on August 28 under P200049/S021. The Canadian classification does not establish a US recall or Amulet 360 applicability.

news.title: Case report describes septal balloon occlusion as a bailout during mitral TEER
news.summary: A single-patient report describes temporary balloon occlusion of an iatrogenic atrial septal defect after profound hypoxemia developed during mitral TEER. A compliant sizing balloon beside the transseptal sheath restored oxygenation while preserving access for PASCAL deployment; definitive septal closure followed. This is an abstract-only procedural case, with no comparative evidence, exact PASCAL generation or disclosed septal-occluder model.

news.title: Acoramidis Shows Real-World Benefit Versus Tafamidis in ATTR-CM
news.summary: A peer-reviewed U.S. claims-data study comparing acoramidis (170 patients) with tafamidis (448 patients) in ATTR-CM found a 34% lower risk of a composite clinical-worsening endpoint (diuretic intensification, HF hospitalization, or death) with acoramidis, and a 43% lower risk of diuretic intensification alone. BridgeBio, which markets acoramidis, sponsored the analysis and cautioned that administrative claims data capture cardiac biomarkers poorly and that the 4.6-month average follow-up is short given acoramidis' recent approval.

news.title: FDA approves PASCAL Ace with Capture Clarity MR implant-system supplement
news.summary: FDA’s PMA record lists September 23 approval of PASCAL Ace with Capture Clarity MR Implant System under P220003/S028, categorized as a design/components/specifications/material change. Detailed labeling and the exact technical changes remain unreviewed; this record does not establish a Capture Clarity tricuspid indication.

news.title: UltraSight announces $24 million Series B2 financing
news.summary: UltraSight announced $24 million in Series B2 financing led by Alive HealthTech Growth Fund to support US expansion and additional cardiac workflows. Echosystem is a product-line/workflow name; FDA acquisition-guidance clearances do not establish automated AS interpretation authorization.

news.title: Corcym reports first-in-human implant of Memo 4D Curve, an open-configuration mitral annuloplasty ring
news.summary: Corcym announced the first human implant of Memo 4D Curve, an FDA-cleared open-configuration addition to its Nitinol Memo mitral annuloplasty family, sized up to 42 mm for annuli ranging from standard degenerative disease to severely dilated. Michael Ibrahim performed the procedure at UVA Health; Corcym said it will formally introduce the ring internationally at the EACTS meeting in October 2026. No comparative outcomes data versus the existing closed Memo 4D ring were disclosed.

news.title: HighLife announces €80 million financing for European expansion and U.S. pivotal development
news.summary: HighLife disclosed a €80 million ($90+ million) financing co-led by Andera Partners, Sofinnova Partners, Supernova Invest and Mérieux Equity Partners. The company plans to expand European commercialization and advance its U.S. pivotal program; its TMVR products remain investigational in the United States.

news.title: UBC's Heart Valve Performance Laboratory reports on a soft-closure mechanical valve prototype
news.summary: The University of British Columbia's Heart Valve Performance Laboratory described the design rationale and pulse-duplicator hydrodynamic testing of iValve, a bileaflet mechanical heart-valve platform built around curved leaflets and distributed, progressive closure contact intended to reduce the rapid-closure flow events linked to mechanical-valve thromboembolism and hemolysis. Prototypes maintained large projected opening areas across 10 test cycles at physiologic flow and pressure conditions. # needs-fulltext: abstract/metadata only, full text is paywalled.

news.title: Respiree adds ARKRAY & PARTNERS and Bizedge Capital to Series A syndicate
news.summary: Respiree announced two additional international investors joining its Series A syndicate, led by We Venture Capital and ClavystBio. The company plans to expand its commercial team and U.S. presence; the release does not disclose the round amount.

news.title: HFSA schedules C-MIC II and III analyses
news.summary: HFSA announced October 12 sessions covering C-MIC II core-laboratory CPET and a C-MIC III pilot comparison with C-MIC II. Programme titles establish scheduled topics; written result abstracts were not located.

news.title: Single-center study links TAVR performed more than 6 months after AS diagnosis to worse outcomes
news.summary: A retrospective single-center study of 149 severe aortic stenosis patients (2021-2023) found the composite of heart-failure hospitalization or death occurred more often when TAVR was performed more than 6 months after diagnosis (n=49) than within 6 months (n=100), over a median 729-day follow-up. Guidelines already call for surveillance within roughly 6-12 months for patients who do not meet immediate-intervention criteria; the authors say the findings support timelier evaluation but call for larger, multicenter confirmation given the small, single-site, non-randomized design.

news.title: Politecnico di Milano validates a balloon post-dilation model for patient-specific TAVI simulation
news.summary: Politecnico di Milano engineers, working with Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico, added a calibrated finite-element balloon model to patient-specific TAVI simulations to reproduce the post-dilation step that earlier simulation pipelines skipped. Predicted post-dilation valve configurations were compared against post-operative CT in four patients, and including the post-dilation step improved agreement between simulated and actual final device geometry. # needs-fulltext: abstract/metadata only, full text is paywalled.

news.title: AI-powered ultrasound robotic system guides transcatheter closure of congenital heart disease in China
news.summary: A Chinese team reported performing a transcatheter closure of an atrial septal defect in a 48-year-old patient using an AI-powered ultrasound robotic system. Public reports describe the platform as combining automated ultrasound acquisition, lesion identification, 3D anatomical reconstruction, path planning, and real-time procedural navigation, while clinicians retained responsibility for the intervention and device deployment.
news.sourceName: Sixth Medical Center of the Chinese PLA General Hospital

news.title: ROS-responsive nanogel coating targets inflammation-driven bioprosthetic valve failure
news.summary: Sichuan University (West China Hospital) researchers compared explanted failed and non-degenerated bioprosthetic heart valves and found pronounced inflammation and reactive-oxygen-species accumulation in the failed leaflets. Guided by that finding, they built a ROS-responsive, diclofenac-releasing zwitterionic nanogel coating for glutaraldehyde-fixed pericardium designed to blunt inflammation-driven degeneration rather than only address calcification directly. # needs-fulltext: abstract/metadata only, full text is paywalled.

news.title: CLOSURE-AF sex-specific analysis raises new caution about LAAO in older women who can tolerate DOAC therapy
news.summary: A sex-specific analysis of the randomized CLOSURE-AF trial found that worse outcomes with LAAO versus best medical therapy were concentrated in women. Among women, the primary composite endpoint occurred in 58.7% with LAAO versus 35.1% with medical therapy, while no comparable adverse treatment effect was seen in men; the strongest interaction involved cardiovascular or unexplained death.

news.title: CMS finalizes expanded Medicare coverage for TAVR, including asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis
news.summary: CMS finalized a major update to the U.S. National Coverage Determination for TAVR. Medicare coverage now extends to selected patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis under coverage-with-evidence-development, while symptomatic severe AS no longer carries that CED requirement. CMS also preserved the multidisciplinary heart-team model while allowing more flexibility in chart-review triage, operator configuration, and volume criteria.

news.title: PEDIAVALVE project reports decellularized pulmonary valves sized for small children
news.summary: A Romania-based team (George Emil Palade University of Medicine, Targu Mures) working with Clemson University's Dan Simionescu published decellularization results for lamb pulmonary valves aimed at right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction in children, a size range under 15mm poorly served by current options. The protocol removed over 90% of donor DNA while preserving the valve's 3D matrix architecture, and decellularized valves matched fresh valves on opening area, pressure gradient, and 14-day cell viability in bench testing.

news.title: Carvolix submits TAVIPILOT Software for CE marking, targeting European launch in early 2027
news.summary: Carvolix announced that it submitted the European regulatory dossier for CE marking of TAVIPILOT Software, its AI-based intraoperative guidance system for TAVR. The software has already received FDA clearance in the United States, and Carvolix now expects a possible CE Mark by year-end 2026 followed by an initial commercial rollout in France and Germany in early 2027.

news.title: Emboline receives FDA clearance for the Emboliner embolic-protection system for TAVR
news.summary: The FDA granted 510(k) clearance to Emboline’s Emboliner Embolic Protection System for use during TAVR. The self-expanding filter is designed to protect all three cerebral vessels while also capturing embolic material that could travel to systemic organs, giving it a broader protection concept than cerebral-only filters.

news.title: Large U.S. study highlights persistent heart-failure risk and underuse of guideline-directed therapy after TAVR
news.summary: An analysis of more than 37,000 U.S. TAVR patients found that heart failure remains common before and after valve replacement and that evidence-based HF medications are frequently underused. Within one year of TAVR, 18.6% experienced an acute HF episode; HF hospitalization and all-cause mortality reached 8.8% and 9.8% at one year, rising to 13.8% and 17.9% at two years.
news.sourceName: Cardiovascular Business / Journal of Cardiovascular Medicine

news.title: Tempus receives ARPA-H award to test an autonomous AI agent in heart failure
news.summary: Tempus said an award of up to $9.5 million will support development and prospective multicenter validation of an AI agent intended to coordinate heart-failure care; the system remains investigational.

news.title: Corcym reports first-in-human implant of TriMemo, a dedicated tricuspid annuloplasty ring
news.summary: Corcym announced the first human implantation of TriMemo, a semi-rigid Nitinol annuloplasty ring purpose-built for tricuspid valve repair rather than adapted from a mitral design, performed by A. Marc Gillinov at Cleveland Clinic. The device received FDA clearance in April 2026 and is now commercially available in the US, extending Corcym's two-decade-old Memo mitral platform to the tricuspid valve; the release does not describe a pivotal trial or patient-selection criteria beyond this first case.

news.title: India launches national Valve Registry for transcatheter valve interventions
news.summary: India launched the India Valve Registry, a collaborative multicenter initiative designed to collect de-identified real-world data on patients undergoing transcatheter valve interventions and their long-term outcomes. The registry aims to generate India-specific evidence rather than relying primarily on European and North American datasets, and participating centers will contribute standardized treatment and outcome information.

news.title: Medividia-affiliated study compares patient-specific post-TAVI simulations with echocardiography
news.summary: An original five-subject SAPIEN 3 Ultra modeling study coupled Abaqus and FlowVision to compare predicted hemodynamics with echocardiography. The preliminary comparison supported further benchmarking, particularly for effective orifice area; it does not establish clinical treatment-selection efficacy.

news.title: InnovHeart completes first U.S. implant of Saturn transseptal TMVR system
news.summary: InnovHeart announced the first U.S. implantation of its Saturn Transseptal TMVR System in the CASSINI-US Early Feasibility Study. The procedure was performed August 25 at NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia in an 86-year-old woman with symptomatic severe functional mitral regurgitation, and the company reported elimination of MR after implantation. Saturn has now been implanted in 15 patients globally, moving the platform from initial international feasibility toward structured U.S.

news.title: LuX-Valve Plus TTVR expands into Eastern India with two high-risk cases
news.summary: Apollo Multispeciality Hospitals in Kolkata reported two consecutive transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement procedures using the Jenscare LuX-Valve Plus system in elderly, frail patients with severe symptomatic TR. Post-procedure assessments reportedly showed satisfactory valve function and resolution of significant regurgitation without major complications.

news.title: Modified transseptal BATMAN technique reported for high-risk mitral valve-in-valve TMVR
news.summary: A three-case series described a modified transseptal BATMAN — Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior leaflet — technique for patients undergoing mitral valve-in-valve TMVR who were at high risk of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. All three complex cases were reported as successful, illustrating another strategy for modifying the anterior mitral leaflet before valve implantation.

news.title: Medtronic invests up to $80M in Pi-Cardia and secures option to acquire the company
news.summary: Medtronic announced a strategic investment of up to $80 million in Pi-Cardia, developer of the FDA-cleared ShortCut leaflet-modification system used to enable valve-in-valve TAVR in patients at risk of coronary obstruction. Medtronic is expected to become the exclusive global commercial distributor for ShortCut in 2027, and the agreement includes an option to acquire Pi-Cardia for an estimated upfront price of up to $210 million, plus potential earn-outs.

news.title: Providence St. Joseph begins commercial use of Edwards SAPIEN M3 TMVR in Orange County
news.summary: Providence St. Joseph Hospital reported the first commercial SAPIEN M3 TMVR procedure in Orange County, California, expanding local access to Edwards Lifesciences’ FDA-approved transseptal mitral-replacement system. SAPIEN M3 is indicated for selected patients with symptomatic moderate-to-severe or severe MR who are unsuitable for surgery or TEER, and also for certain patients with mitral annular calcification.

news.title: C-MIC IV sham-controlled subcutaneous study registered
news.summary: ClinicalTrials.gov posted C-MIC IV, a 60-participant estimated sham-controlled study stratified by ischemic/nonischemic etiology. The record lists not yet recruiting and an estimated September start; no results are posted.

news.title: LAACS-2 finds no significant overall stroke reduction with routine surgical LAA closure, with a high-risk subgroup signal
news.summary: At ESC Congress 2026, investigators reported 1,500 patients randomized during planned open-heart surgery and followed for a median of four years: stroke or TIA occurred in 4.28% assigned LAA closure versus 5.04% with standard care (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.53–1.37; P=0.517). A prespecified report described a 56% reduction in the subgroup above the median CHA2DS2-VASc risk score (P=0.018); this does not establish routine benefit for all surgical patients, and long-term follow-up continues. The surgical technique/device mix was not specified in the press report, so these findings do not establish efficacy for a particular clip generation.

news.title: ACASA-TAVI: ongoing NOAC monotherapy reduces subclinical leaflet thrombosis after TAVR
news.summary: ACASA-TAVI randomized 360 post-TAVR patients to NOAC monotherapy or aspirin and found significantly less hypoattenuated leaflet thickening with anticoagulation. HALT occurred in 16.2% of the NOAC group versus 28.6% of patients receiving aspirin, while the composite safety endpoint of bleeding, thromboembolism or death was noninferior. The result suggests that anticoagulation can materially suppress subclinical valve thrombosis without an obvious safety penalty in this trial population.

news.title: CARDIO-TTRansform subgroup analysis links eplontersen effect to baseline stabilizer use
news.summary: A prespecified CARDIO-TTRansform analysis found that baseline TTR-stabilizer use modified eplontersen’s effect on cardiovascular death/recurrent cardiovascular events. Benefit appeared without a baseline stabilizer (RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.54–0.93), while the stabilizer subgroup showed no benefit (RR 1.14, 0.85–1.53). The overall trial was neutral. This missing August publication is a backfill; the subgroup findings do not establish benefit in the overall study population.

news.title: LUMINARA Phase 2b Trial: Oral Relaxin Agonist AZD5462 Shows Early Promise in Heart Failure
news.summary: In the 375-patient LUMINARA Phase 2b trial, presented as an ESC 2026 Hot Line and published simultaneously in Circulation, AstraZeneca's oral RXFP1 relaxin-receptor agonist AZD5462 modestly improved a cardiac-remodeling measure (end-systolic volume index) in an HFrEF cohort (LVEF <=35%) and lowered systemic vascular resistance in a separate cohort with LVEF 41-55%, without excess hypotension or fluid retention. This was a dose-ranging safety/hemodynamic study, not powered for clinical outcomes, and the investigators said larger outcomes trials are now needed.

news.title: NOTION-4 tempers enthusiasm for short-course anticoagulation solely to prevent HALT
news.summary: NOTION-4 randomized 352 post-TAVR patients without another indication for oral anticoagulation to lifelong single antiplatelet therapy or three months of a DOAC followed by antiplatelet therapy. At three months, HALT was markedly lower with DOAC therapy—12.1% versus 31.8%—but by one year the difference had largely disappeared after anticoagulation was stopped, with HALT rates of 28.3% versus 32.2%.

news.title: REVEAL reports I 124 evuzamitide diagnostic accuracy
news.summary: The published REVEAL 170-person cohort reported 94% sensitivity and 86% specificity for suspected cardiac amyloidosis. This is a diagnostic radiotracer study; Bayer continues to describe the agent as investigational.

news.title: TAVI PCI trial supports TAVR-first as a viable strategy when PCI is also planned
news.summary: The randomized TAVI PCI trial compared TAVI-first versus PCI-first strategies in patients with severe aortic stenosis and concomitant coronary artery disease. At one year, the composite primary endpoint occurred in 22.2% of the TAVI-first group versus 24.2% of the PCI-first group, establishing noninferiority of the TAVI-first approach.

news.title: TRIC-I-HF shows transcatheter tricuspid repair can improve hard clinical outcomes
news.summary: TRIC-I-HF randomized 360 patients with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation and elevated heart-failure risk to transcatheter tricuspid valve repair plus medical therapy or medical therapy alone. At one year, repair was superior on a hierarchical endpoint incorporating death, HF hospitalization and quality-of-life improvement, with a win ratio of 2.42. Longer-term follow-up also showed a lower risk of the composite of death or HF hospitalization through three years.

news.title: HELIOS-B Subgroup Shows Vutrisiran Benefit Holds Regardless of Background Tafamidis
news.summary: A prespecified HELIOS-B subgroup analysis presented at ESC Congress 2026 examined 654 ATTR-CM patients, 40% of whom were on background tafamidis, and found vutrisiran's effect on the composite of all-cause mortality and recurrent cardiovascular events through 33-36 months was consistent whether or not patients also took tafamidis. Alnylam, which markets vutrisiran, noted the trial was not statistically powered specifically for the tafamidis-combination subgroup and that health-status gains were attenuated in that group.

news.title: AI-supported monitoring of patients awaiting TAVI is linked to lower mortality
news.summary: ESC Congress featured new data showing that AI-supported monitoring of patients awaiting TAVI reduced mortality compared with conventional waiting-list management. The presentation sits within a broader ESC session focused on structural-heart imaging, artificial intelligence and procedural optimization, reflecting growing interest in digital tools that extend beyond CT sizing and into longitudinal patient management.

news.title: Bristol Myers Squibb Presents 5-Year Camzyos (Mavacamten) Data From EXPLORER-LTE at ESC 2026
news.summary: In the EXPLORER-LTE cohort of the MAVA-LTE extension study (231 patients followed up to 252 weeks), continuous mavacamten treatment was associated with sustained LVOT-gradient reduction, and 69.6% of patients improved by at least one NYHA class, with no new safety signals versus the original EXPLORER-HCM trial. Seven patients had reversible LVEF drops below 50% that recovered after treatment interruption, and Bristol Myers Squibb noted continued approval still depends on confirmatory post-marketing evidence.

news.title: ESC analyses extend aficamten evidence across obstructive and non-obstructive HCM
news.summary: Cytokinetics reported that ACACIA-HCM analyses showed changes in cardiac structure and diastolic function, while a MAPLE-HCM subgroup analysis favored aficamten over metoprolol across prior-treatment groups.

news.title: ELEM outlines a shared modeling framework for heart-failure research
news.summary: ELEM described research combining patient imaging and ECG data with electromechanical modeling across ischemic cardiomyopathy, obstructive HCM and ATTR-CM. The written research overview stresses validation for each intended use; it does not establish clinical outcome benefit or authorization for treatment selection.

news.title: 2026 ESC Guidelines Redefine Heart Failure Classification, Drop HFmrEF Category
news.summary: The 2026 ESC Guidelines for the management of heart failure, published in the European Heart Journal and presented at ESC Congress 2026, collapse the three-way ejection-fraction classification into two phenotypes -- HFrEF (LVEF <50%) and HFpEF (LVEF >=50%) -- eliminating the separate HFmrEF category, and give mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (e.g., finerenone) a Class I recommendation across the EF spectrum. The guidelines also give semaglutide or tirzepatide a Class IIa recommendation in HFpEF patients with obesity, reflecting trial evidence rather than a formal drug-label change for that indication.

news.title: JAMA study evaluates novice-acquired cardiac ultrasound for AS detection
news.summary: A Mayo diagnostic study combined AI-guided ultrasound acquisition with automated detection of moderate or greater AS. The public abstract reports 1302 prospective novice-operator examinations, with 1258 suitable for automated analysis; sensitivity was 93% and specificity 96%. Exact commercial software releases are unverified.

additionalSources.label: UltraSight disclosure linking the study to its workflow

news.title: Abbott’s Amulet 360 LAA occluder receives CE Mark
news.summary: Abbott received CE Mark approval for Amulet 360, its next-generation dual-seal left atrial appendage occluder for patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. The redesigned lobe is softer and more conformable, with smaller anchors intended to accommodate a broader range of LAA anatomies while retaining the outer disk as a second sealing layer.

publicationDateCorrection.reason: Primary HighLife release is dated August 27; retain the immutable existing News ID.

news.title: HighLife receives CE Mark for Clarity next-generation TMVR valve
news.summary: HighLife announced CE marking for its next-generation Clarity valve, including standard and LAV configurations. Its open-cell outflow design is intended to address LVOTO-related anatomical constraints. Manufacturer claims await independent certificate/label confirmation; U.S. use remains investigational.

news.title: Surgical C-MIC follow-up reports outcomes after deactivation
news.summary: The 31-person uncontrolled C-MIC II follow-up reports persistence of several improvements 12 months after device deactivation; three patients required reactivation. Small sample and absent concurrent control limit interpretation.

news.title: Echopoint announces collaboration with International Heart Spasms Alliance
news.summary: Echopoint announced an IHSA collaboration intended to bring patient input into clinical evaluation and communication for its iKOr coronary physiology program. The announcement does not establish clinical results or marketing authorization.

news.title: Meta-analysis examines combined LAAO and TAVR for patients with atrial fibrillation
news.summary: A new systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated comparative studies of TAVR plus left atrial appendage occlusion versus TAVR followed by standard medical therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation. The clinical question is important because TAVR patients with AF frequently have both high thromboembolic risk and substantial bleeding vulnerability from chronic anticoagulation.

news.title: Radiographics review highlights failure modes in CT-based TAVR planning
news.summary: A new Radiographics review focuses on challenging anatomical and pathological features that can compromise CT segmentation and TAVR planning. The authors emphasize that automated or gradient-based 3D processing can generate erroneous annular, LVOT, root, or vascular-access measurements unless operators recognize and correct artifacts. The work is especially timely as structural-heart planning becomes increasingly automated and AI-assisted.

news.title: New JACC analysis tests how robust the randomized evidence for mitral TEER really is
news.summary: Investigators reassessed COAPT, MITRA-FR, and RESHAPE-HF2 using fragility-index methods to quantify how resistant their conclusions are to small changes in event counts. COAPT’s reductions in heart-failure hospitalization and mortality remained comparatively robust, whereas several nonsignificant MITRA-FR outcomes were statistically fragile.

news.title: National real-world study sharpens the lifetime-management debate after TAVR
news.summary: A retrospective Epic Cosmos analysis included 300,927 TAVR patients treated from 2010 through May 2026 and examined long-term reintervention and clinically significant valve failure. Reintervention remained uncommon—1.2% at 5 years and 2.7% at 10 years—but 3,315 patients underwent redo-TAVR and 347 underwent surgical explantation.

news.title: PREVUE-VALVE shows AI-ECG structural-heart screening loses accuracy when moved into the community
news.summary: The PREVUE-VALVE study tested the EchoNext AI-ECG structural-heart disease model in a community cohort of adults aged 65–85 who received in-home ECG and echocardiography. Among 2,402 analyzable participants, structural-heart disease prevalence was only about 7.5% and the AI model’s discrimination fell to an AUC of 0.71, compared with approximately 0.83 in hospital-based cohorts; performance improved to about 0.79 in people with an abnormal ECG.

news.title: LuX-Valve Plus shows strong early outcomes in patients with very large tricuspid anatomy
news.summary: The European TRINITY cohort reported outcomes in 114 high-risk patients with severe or greater symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation treated using 55–70 mm LuX-Valve Plus systems, specifically addressing patients whose annuli are too large for many competing TTVR platforms. Intraprocedural success was 95.6%, 30-day clinical success was 91.2%, and 93.7% of patients had residual TR of moderate or less at 30 days.

news.title: Automated CT pipeline maps fibrocalcific burden ahead of TAVI
news.summary: Researchers at Vita-Salute San Raffaele University (Milan) built a one-click, CT-based pipeline that automatically segments and quantifies fibrotic and calcific tissue on the aortic valve from pre-TAVI cardiac CT, replacing a manual, radiologist-dependent step. In 25 patients with severe aortic stenosis the automated regional measurements agreed closely with two independent expert readers while processing each case in under three minutes. # needs-fulltext: abstract/metadata only, full text is paywalled.

news.title: Versa Vascular adds $15M to Series C and appoints former Medtronic structural-heart leader as CEO
news.summary: Versa Vascular appointed Bill Shields as CEO and announced a $15 million expansion of its Series C financing, bringing total committed capital in the round to $42 million. Shields previously spent 15 years at Medtronic and most recently led its Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Therapies division. The new funding is earmarked for completion of the ongoing first-in-human study of the AdapTR transcatheter tricuspid repair system, a U.S.

news.title: Jupiter Endovascular recruits structural-heart trial leader to advance its Transforming Fixation catheter platform
news.summary: Jupiter Endovascular appointed interventional cardiologist Catalin Toma as chief medical officer. The company’s Transforming Fixation (TFX) platform is designed to let a catheter transition from flexible to fixed and back again, addressing the trade-off between navigation and procedural stability.

news.title: Review maps engineering path for soft robotic cardiac sleeves in heart failure
news.summary: A UNSW Sydney-led team, with Hannover Medical School, published a Nature Communications review of soft robotic cardiac sleeves, a non-blood-contact class of mechanical circulatory support that wraps and actuates around the outside of the heart. The review lays out the pathophysiological rationale, recent actuator and materials advances, and the engineering and translational hurdles still standing between prototypes and clinical use, and proposes a development framework for future devices.

news.title: Heart 'assembloids' give researchers a lab model of human valve disease
news.summary: University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University researchers combined heart-chamber organoids grown from human stem cells into valve-bearing 'assembloids,' adding simulated blood flow and muscle contraction to reproduce native valve development. Introducing disease-linked mutations reproduced signs of mitral valve prolapse, offering a human tissue model for studying valve disorders without relying solely on animal studies. The work was published in Cell Stem Cell on August 11, 2026.

news.title: EARLY TAVR analysis shows treadmill testing can unmask treatment indications in “asymptomatic” severe AS
news.summary: A prespecified EARLY TAVR registry analysis found that treadmill stress testing identified an established indication for aortic valve replacement in roughly one in six patients initially considered asymptomatic with severe aortic stenosis. Of 1,250 screened patients, 146 had a positive stress test; among registry participants, 75.8% underwent AVR by six months, 79.9% by one year, and 85.9% by two years.

news.title: JACC publishes two-part best-practice framework for redo-TAVR
news.summary: A Heart and Valve Collaboratory consensus effort published a two-part technical framework for redo-TAVR, separating short-frame and tall-frame device combinations and emphasizing that TAV-in-TAV cannot be treated as a generic procedure. The documents standardize CT-based sizing and risk assessment, including implant-depth effects, neoskirt geometry, leaflet overhang, coronary access, sinus sequestration risk, anchoring, and second-valve expansion.

news.title: KU Leuven-led model simulates pulmonary-autograft dilation after the Ross procedure
news.summary: Engineers at KU Leuven, with Eindhoven University of Technology and Ghent University, built an image-based finite-element pipeline that reconstructs patient-specific root geometry and simulates how the pulmonary autograft grows and remodels under systemic pressure after a Ross procedure. The model reproduced observed autograft dilation in a sheep model and linked the predicted diameter change to leaflet coaptation loss, a step toward predicting which autografts will fail and require reoperation.
news.sourceName: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Biomedical Engineering (PMC)

news.title: Asia-Pacific multicenter registry supports BASILICA and UNICORN leaflet modification for high-risk TAVR
news.summary: A multicenter Asia-Pacific registry reported real-world outcomes for transcatheter electrosurgical leaflet-modification techniques used to mitigate coronary obstruction during TAVR, including BASILICA and the newer UNICORN approach. The registry included 100 patients treated across seven centers; BASILICA was used in 67%, UNICORN in 30%, and a combined approach in 3%, with procedural success reported in 85.1% and 96.7% of BASILICA and UNICORN cases, respectively.

news.title: UC Davis performs first U.S. CARLEN procedure in Nyra Medical’s ENHANCE mitral-repair study
news.summary: UC Davis Medical Center reported the first U.S. treatment of symptomatic functional mitral regurgitation with Nyra Medical’s investigational CARLEN System as part of the ENHANCE Early Feasibility Study. CARLEN is a transcatheter, single-leaflet implant intended to restore mitral leaflet coaptation without sutures, tethers, or permanent alteration of the native valve anatomy, potentially preserving future treatment options. The first U.S.

news.title: UC Irvine study evaluates polycarbonate-polyurethane scaffolds for polymeric mitral valves
news.summary: A UC Irvine biomedical engineering team led by Arash Kheradvar compared two polycarbonate-based polyurethanes as trileaflet scaffold materials for polymeric mitral valves, linking rheological and mechanical properties to valve-level flow, pressure, and wear performance out to 50 million accelerated cycles. One formulation was implanted in an ovine model as an early in-vivo check, part of a broader push toward polymeric valves that combine mechanical-valve durability with bioprosthetic-like hemodynamics.

news.title: Daxor announced an eastern Kansas outpatient ezBVA Lab service launch
news.summary: Daxor announced a new outpatient blood-volume analysis program at an unnamed eastern Kansas healthcare facility using its ezBVA Lab send-out model. The release does not identify which BVA analyzer generation was used. Service availability is a commercial milestone, not clinical evidence of improved outcomes.

news.title: Modular robotic steerable catheter platform demonstrates potential for complex endovascular access
news.summary: Researchers described a handheld robotic catheter with two steerable segments and four degrees of freedom, coupled to a modular tendon-driven actuation platform. The prototype was evaluated through simulation and in-vitro vascular-phantom testing for fenestrated and branched endovascular aneurysm repair.

news.title: ACC launches enhanced IMPACT Registry with a dedicated transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement option
news.summary: The American College of Cardiology released an enhanced version of the IMPACT Registry with more flexible data-collection pathways for interventional catheterization, electrophysiology, cardiac implantable electronic devices, and transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement. Programs can now select a submission pathway focused specifically on TPVR, which should reduce data-entry burden while preserving procedure-specific quality tracking.

news.title: TEER-CHINA design paper describes DragonFly-T versus medical therapy in tricuspid regurgitation
news.summary: The TEER-CHINA design publication describes an investigational DragonFly-T tricuspid repair comparison against optimized medical therapy in China. The registry still lists recruiting with estimated enrollment of 236 in its June revision. This is study design and registry status, not a clinical readout or evidence of FDA marketing authorization; exact participant-level clip models are unresolved.

news.title: Rare dual caval valve implantation performed for severe tricuspid regurgitation
news.summary: A multidisciplinary team at the Army Institute of Cardio-Thoracic Sciences in Pune reported a complex minimally invasive procedure in a patient with prior valve surgery and severe tricuspid regurgitation. The team implanted prosthetic valves in both the superior and inferior vena cava, creating a bicaval valve implantation strategy intended to reduce venous backflow without repeat open-heart surgery.

news.title: Edwards reports strong Q2 structural-heart growth and raises TAVR/TMTT guidance
news.summary: Edwards reported Q2 TAVR sales of $1.26 billion, up 11.3% year over year, and transcatheter mitral/tricuspid therapy sales of roughly $196 million, up about 47%. The company raised full-year TAVR growth guidance to 8%–9% and TMTT sales guidance to $760–$780 million. Edwards also highlighted upcoming TCT presentations for PROGRESS and CLASP IITR, expected U.S. approval of PASCAL for tricuspid use in Q4, and expected U.S./European approval of the next-generation PASCAL with Capture Clarity.

news.title: Affinia reports FDA Orphan Drug designation for AFTX-201 in BAG3 DCM
news.summary: Affinia reported FDA Orphan Drug designation for investigational AFTX-201 in BAG3-associated DCM. This sponsor-reported development designation is not marketing authorization. Its July 18–55 eligibility description differs from the September 1 registry and October 9 sponsor description of 18–70; the exact change date is unverified.

news.title: Boston Scientific starts FARADIGM IDE trial for Faraflex PFA system
news.summary: Boston Scientific enrolled the first patients in its FARADIGM IDE trial of the investigational Faraflex pulsed-field ablation catheter, with initial procedures performed at St. David’s Medical Center. Faraflex combines mapping and ablation in a single 8 Fr NAV-enabled catheter used with the Opal HDx mapping system. This is primarily an electrophysiology development rather than a structural-heart therapy milestone, so it is lower priority here.

news.title: Jenscare completes first U.S. implants in TRINITY pivotal TTVR trial
news.summary: Jenscare Scientific completed the first patient implantations in its TRINITY U.S. pivotal trial for the LuX-Valve Plus transvenous tricuspid valve replacement system. The initial cases were performed at Montefiore Hospital, just weeks after the device received CE mark approval in Europe. LuX-Valve Plus is Jenscare’s second-generation TTVR platform for severe tricuspid regurgitation and uses a transvenous delivery approach.

news.title: Professional societies push CMS to preserve heart-team and registry safeguards in TAVR NCD update
news.summary: SCAI, ACC, and STS submitted joint comments supporting modernization of the U.S. TAVR National Coverage Determination while asking CMS to clarify several proposed changes. The groups recommended maintaining multidisciplinary heart-team evaluation, national-registry participation, and targeted coverage-with-evidence-development for selected populations. CMS is expected to issue a final decision around September 15, 2026.

news.title: ElectroWire Medical receives FDA 510(k) clearance for LightningWire transseptal puncture system
news.summary: ElectroWire Medical received FDA 510(k) clearance for LightningWire, an electrosurgical guidewire-based system for transseptal puncture, and is beginning a limited U.S. commercial launch. The company positions the device for procedures including atrial fibrillation ablation, left atrial appendage occlusion, and transcatheter mitral valve repair and replacement.

news.title: ACC, SCAI, and STS submit formal comments on CMS’ proposed TAVR National Coverage Determination update
news.summary: The ACC, SCAI, and STS submitted joint comments to CMS on the proposed revision of the National Coverage Determination for TAVR. The societies support modernization of the policy but argue for preserving multidisciplinary heart-team decision-making, audited national registry participation, consistent quality standards, and continued clinical data collection.

news.title: Edwards Lifesciences and Genesis MedTech agree to $12 million FTC settlement related to JC Medical acquisition
news.summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission announced a proposed $12 million settlement with Edwards Lifesciences and Genesis MedTech over allegations that the companies failed to comply with Hart-Scott-Rodino notification and waiting-period requirements in Edwards’ 2024 acquisition of JC Medical. Edwards is set to pay $10 million and Genesis $2 million, with additional prior-notice obligations included in the settlement.

additionalSources.label: FTC case page and proposed judgment status

news.title: Medtronic issues removal action for certain Harmony transcatheter pulmonary valve delivery catheter lots
news.summary: Medtronic reported a removal action for specified lots of the Harmony Delivery Catheter System. FDA recall Z-2624-2026 covers the delivery catheter and advises checking affected lots; it does not identify a recall of the implanted Harmony valve itself.

additionalSources.label: FDA Harmony Delivery Catheter System Class I recall Z-2624-2026

news.title: Cytokinetics announces ESC 2026 late-breaking aficamten abstracts
news.summary: Cytokinetics announced planned ESC Congress presentations covering ACACIA-HCM and a MAPLE-HCM subgroup analysis, keeping cardiac myosin inhibition in focus ahead of the meeting.

news.title: Acoramidis analysis reports early, sustained kidney markers in ATTR-CM
news.summary: A BridgeBio-reported analysis describes an early reversible eGFR change and lower urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio through follow-up in ATTR-CM; it is supportive evidence, not a change to the approved indication.

news.title: Laplace reports FDA IDE approval for TRIUMPH pivotal TTVR trial
news.summary: Laplace Interventional reported FDA investigational device exemption approval for TRIUMPH. Its June 29 announcement described approximately 400 patients randomized 2:1 against commercial TTVR and a separate registry of up to 150 patients unsuitable for commercial TTVR and suboptimal for T-TEER. The system remains investigational; IDE approval permits a study and is not marketing approval.

news.title: STUN-AF suggests LAA ablation before LAAO may reduce peridevice leaks
news.summary: In the nonrandomized STUN-AF study, patients undergoing concomitant pulsed-field ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion had fewer peridevice leaks when the appendage was ablated before occlusion. The proportion with no leak was higher with LAA ablation at both 4 months and 12 months, and multivariable analysis associated LAA ablation with lower odds of leak.

news.title: First U.S. real-world TriClip data show strong commercial rollout
news.summary: TCTMD reported STS/ACC TVT Registry data for more than 3,000 patients treated with Abbott’s TriClip G4 system at 278 U.S. sites after FDA approval. Device success was 98%, 30-day all-cause mortality was 1.4%, median hospital stay was 1 day, and 96% of patients were discharged home. At 30 days, 87% had moderate-or-less TR and 51% had mild-or-less TR, with substantial improvements in KCCQ score and NYHA class.

news.title: Northwestern describes fluoroscopy-free AF ablation and WATCHMAN implantation workflow
news.summary: A Northwestern Medicine Breakthroughs for Physicians clinical video describes a fluoroscopy-free workflow combining catheter ablation and WATCHMAN implantation; the featured physician reports performing ablation and WATCHMAN procedures without radiation exposure over 15 years. Northwestern dates the item only to July 2026, without a publication day. This is a technique feature, not a comparative clinical study; it reports no controlled outcomes, and does not identify the WATCHMAN generation, so efficacy and generation-specific conclusions cannot be drawn. Source dates this report to July 2026; the exact publication day is unverified.

news.title: GE HealthCare introduces Allia upgrade pathways for existing interventional suites
news.summary: GE HealthCare announced Allia platform upgrade pathways intended to modernize selected legacy Innova and Discovery image-guided therapy systems. While not a structural-heart implant announcement, imaging-room capability is increasingly central to TAVR, TEER, TTVR, LAAO, and complex valve programs. The relevance is operational: hospitals may be able to improve image guidance and procedural workflow without replacing the entire interventional suite.

news.title: Abbott highlights TriClip, Navitor, and Amulet 360 datasets at NY Valves
news.summary: Cardiac Interventions Today reported that Abbott presented first U.S. real-world outcomes for TriClip TEER, along with data on Navitor TAVR for aortic stenosis and Amulet 360 LAA occlusion. The TriClip data overlap with the TCTMD TVT Registry coverage and reinforce the commercial-readiness story for tricuspid repair. The Navitor mention is relevant because it shows Abbott continuing to build its TAVR evidence base while TriClip expands its tricuspid franchise.

news.title: J-Valve transfemoral THV system reports 1-year EFS outcomes in severe AR
news.summary: Cardiac Interventions Today noted 1-year outcomes from an early feasibility study of the investigational J-Valve transfemoral transcatheter heart valve system for symptomatic severe aortic regurgitation. Although the item is just outside the strict June 29–July 5 window, it is highly relevant because native AR remains an underpenetrated TAVR-adjacent indication. The U.S.

news.title: Edwards receives FDA clearance for Ecliptis LAA exclusion system
news.summary: Edwards entered surgical left atrial appendage exclusion with FDA clearance for Ecliptis, a clip-based system intended for use during concomitant cardiac surgery.

news.title: Valgen DragonFly TMVR receives CE Mark for functional MR
news.summary: Cardiac Interventions Today reported that Valgen Medtech’s DragonFly transcatheter mitral valve repair system received European CE Mark approval for functional mitral regurgitation. This is outside the strict weekly window but close enough to matter for trend context, especially because transcatheter mitral repair remains a key competitive category. CE Mark approval in FMR indicates continued geographic and technology diversification beyond MitraClip/PASCAL-like incumbent systems.

news.title: CMS proposes major TAVR coverage update
news.summary: CMS proposed removing the coverage-with-evidence-development requirement for TAVR in symptomatic severe aortic stenosis, while expanding coverage to asymptomatic severe AS under CMS-approved evidence-development studies. The proposal also revises patient-assessment, heart-team, operator, hospital, and program-volume requirements. The public-comment period runs through July 15, 2026; the proposal is not yet final.

news.title: FDA lists Class II recall for specified HeartMate 3 LVAS kits
news.summary: FDA posted an open Class II recall initiated May 13, 2026, for specified 11V lithium-ion backup batteries within HeartMate 3 LVAS kits model 106524US (recall Z-2518-2026). Only affected serial-numbered units are covered; the action is not a blanket recall of all implanted HeartMate 3 pumps.

news.title: Cardiawave begins routine European use of Valvosoft, a noninvasive ultrasound therapy for severe symptomatic AS
news.summary: Cardiawave announced routine clinical use of Valvosoft in France, the Netherlands, and Germany following CE marking in late 2025. The company says the system uses high-intensity ultrasound pulses to fragment calcification on native aortic-valve leaflets without surgery, implantation, or general anesthesia.

news.title: MassDevice frames the CMS proposal as a volume tailwind for major TAVR players
news.summary: MassDevice reported that analysts saw the CMS proposal as a positive for Edwards and the broader TAVR category, including Medtronic and Abbott; it also noted Boston Scientific’s potential re-entry via its MiRus investment. The article emphasized the removal of CED for symptomatic patients and the addition of a CED pathway for asymptomatic severe AS.

news.title: PREVUE-VALVE publication reinforces the scale of underrecognized valve disease
news.summary: PREVUE-VALVE used CVS and Walgreens outreach followed by at-home ECG and echocardiography in a national sample of adults aged 65–85. The study estimated moderate-or-greater valvular heart disease in 8.2% of this population and mild-to-moderate disease in 18.4%; tricuspid regurgitation was the most common moderate-or-greater lesion, followed by aortic stenosis and mitral regurgitation.

news.title: Ten-year PARTNER 2A and Sapien 3 registry data sharpen the TAVI durability discussion
news.summary: Ten-year follow-up showed that intermediate-risk patients treated with the older Sapien XT valve in PARTNER 2A had higher mortality and valve reintervention than surgical AVR overall, driven largely by transthoracic-access cases. In contrast, a propensity-matched comparison of the newer Sapien 3 registry cohort versus surgical AVR showed no difference in 10-year all-cause mortality or aortic-valve reintervention.

news.title: Anteris positions DurAVR around lifetime management and disease modification
news.summary: Anteris argued that as TAVR expands to younger, lower-risk patients, success metrics should extend beyond a technically successful implant to include hemodynamics, residual disease physiology, ventricular recovery, durability, and future intervention options. Its DurAVR is a balloon-expandable, single-piece biomimetic THV designed to mimic native-valve flow and is being studied in the PARADIGM trial against commercially available TAVR systems.

news.title: TRISCEND II analysis quantifies hospital-cost and length-of-stay drivers after Evoque TTVR
news.summary: A TRISCEND II analysis of 155 patients undergoing Edwards Evoque transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement found index-admission costs of about $80,005, including a $49,000 device-acquisition cost. New renal-replacement therapy and new pacemaker/CIED implantation were the largest independent contributors to incremental cost, while renal replacement, stroke, and new pacemaker/CIED implantation had the largest effects on length of stay.

news.title: ClinicalTrials.gov lists CORCINCH-HF as suspended
news.summary: The registry's June 2026 update lists the pivotal AccuCinch trial as suspended, with estimated enrollment 400. This is a study-status update and does not establish that the device itself was withdrawn or explain the reason for suspension.

news.title: HEAL-LAA reports six-month outcomes for WATCHMAN FLX Pro in 500-patient post-market study
news.summary: In a prospective, single-arm study at 32 U.S. centers, 500 patients received WATCHMAN FLX Pro; the six-month composite of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding was 11.1% (55/496), below the prespecified 21% performance goal. The primary paper also reports 45-day seal and 12-month follow-up, but the comparison is against performance goals rather than a randomized control, and the study was sponsored by Boston Scientific.

news.title: Boston Scientific announces MiRus investment and conditional SIEGEL TAVR acquisition option
news.summary: Boston Scientific announced a MiRus investment and an option to acquire its TAVR business, subject to milestones and further payments. The disclosure describes investigational SIEGEL sizes of 23, 26 and 29 mm and an 8 Fr expandable sheath. It also references unnamed mitral/tricuspid replacement assets; their materials are unverified. An option is not a completed acquisition, and the system was not commercially approved at the disclosure date.

news.title: MiRus reports first patient treatments in the randomized STAR study of SIEGEL TAVR
news.summary: MiRus reported first treatments in STAR, a randomized comparison of SIEGEL with commercially available TAVR for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis. The registered target is an estimated 1,025 participants; the primary endpoint combines all-cause death, all stroke and valve/procedure-related cardiovascular rehospitalization at one year. The registry revision posted April 9, 2026 lists recruiting and no results. Trial authorization is distinct from commercial valve approval.

news.title: CHAMPION-AF finds WATCHMAN FLX noninferior to NOACs for efficacy and superior for nonprocedural bleeding at three years
news.summary: In the 3,000-patient randomized CHAMPION-AF trial of patients eligible for long-term anticoagulation, WATCHMAN FLX met noninferiority for the composite of cardiovascular death, stroke, or systemic embolism at three years (5.7% vs 4.8%) and reduced nonprocedural major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (10.9% vs 19.0%). The study population had low mean bleeding risk; ischemic stroke was numerically more frequent with closure (3.2% vs 2.0%), and five-year follow-up is ongoing, so this result does not establish broad first-line equivalence for every AF population.

news.title: CLOSURE-AF finds LAA closure did not meet noninferiority versus physician-directed medical therapy in high-risk AF
news.summary: The randomized German CLOSURE-AF trial enrolled 912 patients at high risk of both stroke and bleeding. At median three-year follow-up, the composite of stroke, systemic embolism, major bleeding, or cardiovascular/unexplained death occurred at 16.8 versus 13.3 events per 100 patient-years with closure versus medical therapy; the prespecified noninferiority criterion was not met (P=0.44). The study included physician-selected devices and medical treatment, and its result applies to this older, high-risk population rather than establishing comparative performance for a specific device generation.

news.title: VERITAS reports early procedural and seal outcomes for investigational Amulet 360
news.summary: The prospective, single-arm VERITAS study implanted Amulet 360 in 400 patients at 34 sites; 399 implants succeeded, and all 376 patients with 45-day echocardiography met the seal endpoint of leak ≤5 mm, with 94% complete occlusion and no leak ≥3 mm. Seven-day/discharge safety endpoint events were zero, while device-related thrombus was observed in 2.4% and 3.3% had a major bleed during follow-up. The study has no randomized comparator or demonstrated stroke-reduction efficacy, and the device was investigational in this report.
news.sourceName: Journal of the American College of Cardiology: Clinical Electrophysiology

news.title: ACC Registry study finds machine learning modestly improves prediction of in-hospital LAAO events
news.summary: A JACC: Advances analysis trained and validated logistic regression, LASSO, and XGBoost models on 81,703 procedures in the ACC LAAO Registry. XGBoost discrimination for composite in-hospital major adverse events was modest (validation AUC 0.648 using 16 variables and 0.653 with 51 variables), and performance for rare events remained poor with overfitting concerns; the findings support further registry risk-model development, not a validated bedside decision tool.

news.title: Ancora reports two-year early-study follow-up for AccuCinch LV restoration
news.summary: Ancora announced two-year follow-up from early AccuCinch studies, describing sustained reverse remodeling and improvements in heart function, quality of life, and heart-failure hospitalizations. These are early-study findings reported by the manufacturer; CORCINCH-HF remains the separate randomized pivotal evaluation and AccuCinch is investigational.

news.title: OPINION trial finds no significant one-year benefit from prophylactic surgical LAA closure in patients without prior AF
news.summary: In a 2,118-patient randomized trial of people without preoperative AF undergoing valve surgery, the primary composite of ischemic stroke, TIA, or cardiovascular death occurred in 6.9% with concomitant surgical LAA closure and 8.2% without it (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.61–1.14; P=0.25). A possible signal in the CHA2DS2-VASc ≥3 subgroup is exploratory; follow-up is being extended. The intervention was surgical suture excision/closure, not a comparison of named marketed clip devices, so the results should not be assigned to AtriClip or another specific device.

news.title: FDA expands WATCHMAN FLX and FLX Pro labeling to patients after AF ablation
