news.summary: FDA approved PMA supplement S074 to expand the WATCHMAN FLX and FLX Pro indications to include patients following catheter ablation for non-valvular AF and to add a post-implant drug regimen. The change is specific to the two named FLX generations and their labeled eligibility criteria; it does not extend to the original WATCHMAN or other LAA closure devices.

additionalSources.label: FDA Summary of Safety and Effectiveness Data

news.title: Three-year SWISS-APERO follow-up finds no significant intention-to-treat ischemic difference between Amulet and Watchman/FLX
news.summary: In this 221-patient randomized trial of higher-risk AF patients, the three-year composite of cardiovascular death, stroke, TIA, or systemic embolism was 18.2% with Amulet versus 31.0% with Watchman/FLX (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.33–1.03; P=0.06) in the intention-to-treat analysis. As-treated and per-protocol analyses reached nominal significance, but those findings are hypothesis-generating; the trial was not powered for clinical outcomes, and most Watchman-arm patients received FLX.
news.sourceName: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

news.title: ACC Registry comparison associates WATCHMAN FLX with fewer one-year events than first-generation WATCHMAN
news.summary: A propensity-matched NCDR LAAO Registry analysis compared 27,141 WATCHMAN FLX recipients with 27,141 first-generation WATCHMAN recipients from 641 U.S. sites. At one year, FLX was associated with lower adjusted hazards of major adverse events (HR 0.84), ischemic stroke (HR 0.82), and ischemic stroke/systemic embolism (HR 0.74); 45-day peridevice leak was also lower (14.7% vs 23.5%), while device-related thrombus was similar. This was an observational comparison across different treatment eras, so residual confounding remains possible.

news.title: Amulet IDE analysis finds fewer high-risk thrombi with Amulet than WATCHMAN 2.5
news.summary: A core-laboratory analysis of the randomized Amulet IDE cohort found high-risk device-related thrombus through 12 months in 4.0% of WATCHMAN 2.5 recipients (35/885) versus 2.2% with Amulet (20/903; P=0.030); high-risk thrombus was often detected after 45 days. Across device groups, patients with high-risk DRT had more five-year stroke/systemic embolism/cardiovascular-death events than those with low-risk or no DRT (30.4% vs 19.9%). This post-randomization subgroup analysis does not prove device-related causation or apply to WATCHMAN FLX/FLX Pro.

news.title: ALIVE trial finds no significant 12-month clinical benefit for Revivent TC
news.summary: In a prospective 2:1 device-versus-control study of patients with prior anterior MI and LV remodeling, Revivent TC safely reduced LV dimensions but did not improve the 12-month hierarchical composite efficacy endpoint (win ratio 1.13; P=0.32). A post hoc surgical-only subgroup appeared more favorable and needs randomized confirmation.

news.title: FDA grants De Novo authorization to LSI Solutions Mi-CHORD system
news.summary: FDA granted De Novo DEN230069 for the Mi-CHORD artificial chordae surgical replacement system. Its supporting prospective OUS feasibility cohort enrolled 12 patients with one-year follow-up; that small cohort supports classification and authorization but does not establish comparative effectiveness.

news.title: KISS registry compares transcatheter and surgical paravalvular leak closure
news.summary: In a retrospective three-center cohort of 335 patients, technical success was 78.9% with transcatheter closure and 76.2% with surgery; long-term mortality did not differ significantly. AVP III accounted for 140 of 171 transcatheter cases, so these outcomes are not specific to one device.
news.sourceName: Journal of the American Heart Association

news.title: Multicenter Occlutech PLD study reports sustained improvement after paravalvular leak closure
news.summary: The study enrolled 144 patients at 21 sites; its 112-patient full-analysis set had procedural success of 91.3% for mitral and 90.0% for aortic leaks. At two years, among the reported follow-up subset, NYHA III/IV fell from 80% at baseline to 14.1%; 3 device embolizations were reported. This was nonrandomized and follow-up was incomplete.

news.title: TRICENTO registry reports early results of a custom bicaval valved stent
news.summary: A multicenter retrospective registry of 21 high-risk patients reported 100% technical success and no in-hospital deaths; 3 patients had asymptomatic stent fractures, median follow-up was 61 days, and one-year survival was 76%. The small cohort supports feasibility and highlights a design durability issue.

news.title: Peer-reviewed review reports CorCap was withdrawn from the market
news.summary: A 2021 review states that the CorCap cardiac support device was withdrawn from the market, citing concerns about long-term pericardial constriction. This is a secondary literature report; it does not establish a formal FDA recall or the date withdrawal occurred.

news.title: TRICAVAL trial of caval Sapien XT implantation terminated for safety concerns
news.summary: ClinicalTrials.gov records TRICAVAL as terminated for safety concerns after enrolling 28 participants. This halt concerns inferior caval implantation of Edwards SAPIEN XT in that study; it does not establish a class-wide stop for later bicaval systems such as TricValve.

news.title: PEERLESS-HF stopped after interim futility analysis
news.summary: The randomized HeartNet study was stopped after interim analysis showed the primary six-month efficacy endpoint was unlikely to be met; the trial registry also lists termination. This is a halted trial signal, not evidence that all epicardial restraint therapies were withdrawn.

news.title: FDA grants original PMA to HeartMate II LVAS for bridge to transplantation
news.summary: FDA granted original PMA P060040 for the HeartMate II LVAS as bridge-to-transplantation support in advanced refractory left ventricular failure. Later label supplements expanded indications; the 2008 decision is the initial authorization record.

entity.name: Atrial Fibrillation
entity.description: Most common sustained arrhythmia; thrombus typically forms in the left atrial appendage, the target of LAA closure for stroke prevention when anticoagulation is unsuitable.

entity.name: Patent Foramen Ovale (PFO-associated stroke)
entity.description: Residual interatrial communication implicated in paradoxical embolism and cryptogenic stroke; transcatheter closure reduces recurrent stroke in selected patients.

entity.name: Atrial Septal Defect
entity.description: Congenital opening in the atrial septum causing left-to-right shunt; secundum defects are amenable to transcatheter closure.

entity.name: Ventricular Septal Defect
entity.description: Congenital communication in the ventricular septum or, rarely, acquired septal rupture after myocardial infarction. Management depends on anatomy and hemodynamics; transcatheter closure is used for selected congenital defects and is an evolving option in some post-infarction cases.

entity.name: Patent Ductus Arteriosus
entity.description: Persistent fetal vessel connecting the aorta and pulmonary artery. Management depends on hemodynamic significance and patient age; in preterm infants, the benefits and timing of closure remain debated, with transcatheter closure considered for selected persistent hemodynamically significant cases.

entity.name: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
entity.description: Sarcomeric cardiomyopathy with LV hypertrophy; the obstructive form (HOCM) features dynamic LVOT obstruction treated by septal reduction or cardiac myosin inhibitors.

entity.name: Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy
entity.description: Infiltrative cardiomyopathy from misfolded transthyretin (wild-type or hereditary) depositing in the myocardium; treated with TTR stabilizers and silencers.

data.label: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction

entity.name: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
entity.description: Heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% or less, managed with guideline-directed medical and device therapies tailored to the clinical profile.

data.label: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction

entity.name: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
entity.description: Heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction of 50% or greater and evidence of elevated filling pressures. Current treatment is guided by clinical phenotype and contemporary heart-failure recommendations.

entity.name: Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction & Refractory Angina
entity.description: Angina from impaired microvascular function (often with non-obstructive coronaries); device approaches include coronary sinus narrowing to redistribute perfusion.

entity.name: Aortic Stenosis
entity.description: Progressive narrowing of the aortic valve (commonly calcific/degenerative); severe symptomatic disease is treated by TAVR or surgical AVR, with trials now extending TAVR to low-risk and asymptomatic patients.

curation.notes: CMS finalized the NCD on 2026-09-10: Medicare covers TAVR for symptomatic severe AS without the former CED requirement, while asymptomatic severe AS remains covered only under CED in a CMS-approved study and with a device FDA-approved for that indication. This does not create unrestricted asymptomatic coverage. The 2026-06 proposed-NCD articles retained from the prior note are historical only.

entity.name: Aortic Regurgitation
entity.description: Diastolic backflow through an incompetent aortic valve causing LV volume overload; historically surgical, now with the first dedicated transcatheter device (JenaValve Trilogy) for symptomatic severe AR.

entity.name: Mitral Regurgitation
entity.description: Systolic backflow through the mitral valve, either primary/degenerative (leaflet/chordal) or secondary/functional (annular dilation, LV remodeling); treated by transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER), transcatheter replacement (TMVR), annuloplasty, or surgery.

entity.name: Mitral Stenosis
entity.description: Obstruction to LA-to-LV inflow, most often rheumatic (commissural fusion) or degenerative with mitral annular calcification; treated by percutaneous balloon commissurotomy or surgery.

entity.name: Tricuspid Regurgitation
entity.description: Backflow through the tricuspid valve, frequently functional from annular dilation/right-heart remodeling; long undertreated, now addressed by transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TriClip) and transcatheter replacement (EVOQUE).

entity.name: Pulmonary Valve Disease
entity.description: Pulmonary regurgitation/stenosis or RVOT conduit dysfunction, often in repaired congenital heart disease (e.g. tetralogy of Fallot); treated by transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement (Melody, Harmony) or surgery.

entity.name: Prosthetic paravalvular leak
entity.description: Regurgitant flow through a defect between a prosthetic valve and the native annulus, potentially causing heart failure or hemolysis; selected high-risk patients may undergo transcatheter closure.

entity.name: Ischemic left ventricular remodeling
entity.description: LV dilation and geometric distortion after extensive myocardial infarction; selected patients have been studied for surgical or hybrid scar exclusion and ventricular reconstruction.

entity.name: Systemic hypertension
entity.description: Persistently elevated systemic blood pressure is a cardiovascular risk condition that can cause target-organ injury, including left ventricular remodeling. Diagnosis requires confirmation using repeated or out-of-office blood-pressure measurements; the 2024 ESC guideline defines hypertension as office systolic pressure at least 140 mmHg or diastolic pressure at least 90 mmHg.

entity.name: Heart failure
entity.description: Broad heart failure scope used for LINK-HF2, whose registry eligibility does not restrict to one ejection-fraction subtype.

curation.notes: Broad HF taxonomy candidate. Do not substitute HFrEF-only or HFpEF-only eligibility or assert subtype outcomes. Registry eligibility NYHAII–IV, adult participants.

entity.name: BAG3 Mutation-Associated Dilated Cardiomyopathy
entity.description: BAG3 mutation-associated dilated cardiomyopathy. UPBEAT targets adults with a truncating BAG3 mutation, LVEF below45% and NYHAII/III symptoms; this genotype-specific condition does not stand for all HFrEF.

curation.notes: New genotype-specific condition candidate. Curator should confirm if this belongs in existing condition taxonomy or whether a broader DCM node is preferred; do not map to HFrEF alone.

data.label: Cardiac Performance System (CPS)

entity.name: Cardiac Performance System (CPS)
entity.regulatoryDetail: The company states CPS is investigational, under clinical evaluation under an FDA Investigational Device Exemption, and not approved for commercial use. The company home page labels ejection fraction as FDA approved 2018 and its NIH award abstract says a 510(k) clearance was granted for ejection-fraction measurement (sponsor statements). The FDA record found (510(k) K173156, decision 2018-06-08) is for an Integrated CardioRespiratory System from Sensydia, Inc. indicated for an estimate of left ventricular ejection fraction; no opened document ties it to the Cardiac Performance System.
entity.mechanism: Disposable sensors acquire heart sounds and ECG; proprietary algorithms compute hemodynamic measures such as ejection fraction, cardiac output, pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (company description; algorithm details not reviewed).

The company presents CPS for heart-failure decision points (sponsor wording). A registered observational method-comparison study against right heart catheterization exists (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06870591).

curation.notes: Heart failure is the platform's applicant-described application; the registry lists the condition as Cardiovascular Diseases and the 2018 FDA record carries no heart-failure claim. Trial NCT06870591 is not drafted as a public trial because its registry condition (Cardiovascular Diseases) maps to no existing condition without transferring the heart-failure application.

entity.name: Pivot Bridge

entity.description: In a 2026 first-in-human report (abstract only), 15 patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation who were surgical candidates received the device for a median of 5 days: procedural success in all, no serious adverse events during device placement and a tricuspid regurgitation reduction of at least one grade in all. The device was then removed (10 patients by surgery, 5 percutaneously). This is a short-term implantation cohort, not a Pivot Extend result.

curation.notes: Abstract and funding field of the paper read; full text not opened. The paper states that Tau Medical supplied the devices.

entity.name: ACASA-TAVI
entity.primaryEndpoint: Co-primary endpoints at 12 months: CT-detected hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT; superiority) and a composite of VARC-3 bleeding, thromboembolic events, and all-cause death (noninferiority).
entity.outcomeSummary: In patients aged 65-80 without an independent anticoagulation indication after TAVI, 12 months of factor Xa DOAC monotherapy reduced HALT versus aspirin (16.2% vs 28.6%; risk ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.37-0.82; P=0.004) and met noninferiority for the safety composite (7.5% vs 10.6%). These findings do not establish improved long-term valve durability or superiority for clinical events.

curation.notes: Procedure-level post-TAVI management evidence: the proc-tavi edge identifies the care setting, not a randomized comparison of TAVI devices or TAVI versus surgery. The registry permits clinician-selected therapeutic-dose apixaban, rivaroxaban, or edoxaban monotherapy versus aspirin 75 mg/day; it does not establish separate efficacy for each drug. The ClinicalTrials.gov record last updated June 9, 2026 reports completed status, actual enrollment of 360, and actual start December 4, 2021. It also lists 5- and 10-year MACE follow-up; those results are not reported here. JAMA reports 336 participants completing the trial. The safety risk difference was -3.3 percentage points (95% CI -9.5 to 2.8; noninferiority P<0.001). Low safety-event counts limit inference, and individual clinical components were not adequately powered. HALT is an imaging endpoint; do not generalize the result to all ages, anticoagulation regimens, or routine treatment recommendations.
